sections.heading: C — The Vermont point system
sections.markdown:
## C — The Vermont point system

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Each finding of guilt for breaking a motor vehicle law adds points to your driving record [A01].
Why it matters: Points follow a finding of guilt, not a ticket alone.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Speeding carries two to eight points depending on how far over the limit you were driving [A01].
Why it matters: A range, not a fixed value.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Texting while driving carries two to five points [A01].
Why it matters: Texting has its own range.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Driving without a license carries two points, and failing to stop for a stop sign or red light also carries two points [A01].
Why it matters: Two common two point offenses.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
Failing to obey a police officer carries four points, and failing to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian in a crosswalk also carries four points [A01].
Why it matters: Two four point offenses.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
Failing to yield the right-of-way to an ambulance, fire truck or police officer carries five points [A01].
Why it matters: Emergency vehicle yield failure is five points.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Failing to stop for a school bus stopped with its red warning lights flashing carries five points [A01].
Why it matters: School bus passing is five points.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
When a driver accumulates ten points a letter is sent announcing that the driving privilege will be suspended, and the driver may request a hearing to verify the convictions and the point count [A01].
Why it matters: Ten points triggers the letter and a hearing right.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
The number of points received within two years determines how long the driving privilege is suspended, and more points mean a longer suspension [A01].
Why it matters: The two year window sets the length.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
Points are not assessed for parking violations or defective equipment violations [A01].
Why it matters: Two no point categories.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-vt-class-std:vermont-department-of-motor-vehicles-age:handbook:pdf-0065]

Misconceptions:
- A parking ticket adds points: false, parking and defective equipment violations carry no points.
- Ten points means an automatic fixed suspension: false, ten points brings a suspension letter and a hearing right, and the length depends on points within two years.
- All speeding is the same number of points: false, speeding runs from two to eight points depending on speed over the limit.
- Failing to yield to a pedestrian equals failing to yield to an ambulance: false, the pedestrian offense is four points and the emergency vehicle offense is five.

Mnemonics:
- Two, two, four, four, five, five: license and red light, officer and crosswalk, emergency vehicle and school bus.
- Ten triggers, two years measures: the suspension letter and the window that sets its length.

Glossary:
- Point system: the Vermont record that adds points for each motor vehicle conviction and suspends the privilege at ten
- Suspension hearing: the hearing a driver may request after the ten point letter to verify the convictions and point total
- Defective equipment violation: a vehicle condition offense that carries no points

Dynamic facts isolated:
- None: every rule in this section is stable handbook law for the pined edition; no officeholder, date or fee amount is carried as knowledge.
